Hi John — great talking earlier. Summary and answers below, plus next steps and attachments.

High-level: Redwood supports Private (VPC/on-prem) air-gapped installs via an offline bundle and operator-run upgrade process. We work with customer infra teams to provide signed artifacts, an install image, and an ops runbook.

Answers to your questions:
1) Hardware baseline
 - Minimum (small pilot): 2 x A10G / H100-class GPUs, 256GB RAM, 4–8 CPU cores per node, 4TB NVMe for model cache (recommended).
 - Production (multi-node): 4+ GPUs per node typically; we recommend NVMe for lower latency KV cache; SATA is acceptable for long-term model storage but will add I/O latency.
 - Attached: legacybank-hw-requirements-v2.xlsx with recommended configs and scaling guidance.

2) Offline upgrades & OS patches
 - We provide signed offline bundles for Redwood runtime upgrades and model artifacts. Customer downloads via secure portal or we provide via SFTP/physical media.
 - Upgrade runbook: we support a staged upgrade process (staging node -> canary -> full) executed offline. Runbook includes checksum verification, artifact signing checks, and rollback steps. See attached redwood-private-airgap-checklist.pdf.

3) KMS / key management
 - We support customer-managed KMS/HSMs. Typical flow: customer provisions keys in their HSM, we configure Redwood to use the HSM endpoint via mTLS, and key rotation is handled by the customer; we provide guidance for key rollover with zero downtime in the runbook.

4) Install & maintenance ops
 - IPMI/iLO is helpful for hardware-level troubleshooting but not strictly required. We can operate via an SSH bastion if your security policy prefers that. For air-gapped installs we recommend a dedicated ops VLAN and an out-of-band management plane.

Proposed next steps:
 - Marcus to host a 30-min sizing + runbook walkthrough with Raj and your infra team.
 - We will share the offline bundle checklist, signed artifact process, and the hardware spreadsheet (attached).
 - Please confirm if you want Redwood to provide the initial offline bundle on encrypted USB (we can ship) or via SFTP.

I attached the following: legacybank-hw-requirements-v2.xlsx, network-diagram-redwood-deploy.png, redwood-private-airgap-checklist.pdf

> - For OS updates: can Redwood's offline bundle include signed OS packages (or do we need to spin our own minimal mirror)? Our preference is a deterministic upgrade image we can approve once.
> - For the KMS flow: what specific HSM vendors do you validate against (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Gemalto)?
> - For hardware: do you require IPMI for the initial install so your team can help validate GPU firmware? If IPMI is a must, we'll need to carve out IPMI access policies.

Hi Raj — happy to clarify. TL;DR: we can support both approaches depending on your security posture.

1) Offline OS packages
 - We typically provide a signed, minimal appliance image (OCI/tar) that contains the Redwood runtime + vetted OS packages. Customers can choose to: (a) accept our signed image; (b) mirror the packages internally and sign them themselves. We will provide SHA256 checksums and PGP-sign the release artifacts.

2) HSM compatibility
 - We have validated integrations with: Thales Luna, AWS CloudHSM (when reachable via a customer-managed VPC endpoint), and common KMIP-compliant HSMs (Gemalto, Utimaco). We'll share the compatibility matrix in the doc bundle.

3) IPMI / firmware checks
 - IPMI is strongly recommended for initial firmware validation and remote troubleshooting. If policy prevents external IPMI access, we can adopt a process where your on-call infra engineer executes validation steps locally while we guide via the runbook.

4) Rack / power guidance
 - For 4x H100 per node, plan for ~6–8kW per rack depending on PSU and cooling; we recommend 20–25% headroom for failover and maintenance. We'll include an appliance-level sizing sheet in the hw spreadsheet.

Proposed action: I'll run the 30-min runbook & sizing session on Friday 10:00am PT (Marissa — please confirm). In that session I'll share a sample signed artifact, the HSM compatibility notes, and the step-by-step offline upgrade checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.
